title: A 12-Month Commercial Lease Planning Checklist for Newcastle Businesses
excerpt: Use 12 months as a working planning horizon, then check your actual lease dates. Build a renewal or relocation brief with clear costs, responsibilities and next steps.
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Planning Checklist Newcastle | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Plan a Newcastle commercial lease renewal or relocation around your actual notice dates, workplace brief, occupancy costs and decision responsibilities.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
## When should you start planning a commercial lease renewal?

Start by checking the dates and requirements in your actual lease. Twelve months can be a useful working horizon for organising a renewal or relocation, but it is not a universal notice period, legal deadline or guarantee of negotiating leverage. Your lease provisions, business plans and project complexity determine what needs to happen when.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, the useful question is: which decisions must be made before the next fixed date? Ask your solicitor to confirm notice requirements and record uncertain dates as questions to resolve.

## First, build a reliable dates register

Gather the signed lease, amendments, renewal correspondence and any relevant plans. Record the expiry date, option notice dates if applicable, rent review dates and your desired operating date. Do not calculate a notice deadline from an example in an article.

Use the [critical dates tool](/tools/critical-dates) to organise confirmed information. It is a planning aid; have your solicitor check the dates and the required form of any notice against the documents.

**Helpful tip:** give each date an owner and a source document. An unverified date should remain visibly unverified until checked.

## Use a flexible planning sequence

The stages below describe an order of work, not fixed periods that apply to every lease. Some decisions will overlap, and an approaching deadline may require a different sequence.

| Planning stage | Useful action | Decision to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Establish the position | Confirm lease dates, documents and decision makers | What needs attention first? |
| Clarify the business brief | Record attendance, activities, location and growth assumptions | Can the current premises support the plan? |
| Compare alternatives | Set out renewal and relocation assumptions on the same basis | Which options deserve further investigation? |
| Test delivery requirements | Identify fit out, furniture, IT, access and possible disruption | What would need to happen before the team can operate? |
| Agree the next step | Confirm scope, approval owners and adviser inputs | Who can approve the commercial decision and when? |

If you have less than 12 months, share the dates you know rather than assuming it is too late to ask for help. YOS can discuss the brief and information needed; the available options depend on your circumstances.

## Check whether staying still works

List what the current space supports well and what has become difficult. Consider team attendance, meeting capacity, storage, visitor access and how the business expects to work. Separate essential requirements from preferences.

A renewal can still involve changes to the workplace. Record those costs and disruption assumptions rather than treating staying as a zero-cost option.

[Prepare a Newcastle tenant representation brief](/blog/tenant-representation-brief-newcastle)

## Compare occupancy costs and transition costs separately

Gather current rent and available outgoings information. For each alternative, record the basis of the figures, whether GST is included, any proposed incentives and assumptions that still need verification. Keep initial works, furniture, moving, possible overlap between sites and existing lease exit obligations visible as separate items.

Use the [lease comparison tool](/resources/lease-comparison) to organise the options, then identify anything outside the tool's scope. Estimates and proposed terms need checking before they become an approved business budget.

[Work through the renewal or relocation decision](/blog/renew-or-relocate-commercial-lease)

## Connect the premises decision with delivery

Before committing to another space, identify the workplace changes it may need. Access arrangements, landlord requirements, consultant inputs, appointed contractors, furniture lead times and IT changeovers can affect the delivery plan.

YOS provides [client-side office FitOut project management](/office-fitout), coordinating the agreed client workstream. Appointed contractors perform construction and trade work; the management scope is agreed separately.

**Helpful tip:** work backwards from the date the business needs to operate, and mark the decisions that other tasks depend on. Do not assume the lease commencement date and operational readiness date are the same.

## Make the first conversation useful

Bring what you already know: the premises location, lease dates, current costs and whether you are considering renewal, relocation or both. Flag missing documents and uncertain assumptions. You do not need a fully resolved brief to begin.

[Explore Newcastle tenant representation](/tenant-rep/newcastle) for the local briefing process, or [compare Tenant Rep packages](/tenant-rep#packages) to understand scope and fees.
